A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D2D research. The main text, figures, tables, scoring description, and Appendices A and B are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, robustness experiments, case analysis, and full-dataset results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original benchmark evaluations and supplementary empirical analyses, including Appendix A results.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 and Appendix B retain the same agents, five-stage debate, memory summaries, prompts, and scoring procedure. Figure 2 reorganizes their depiction without establishing an operational change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Weibo21, FakeNewsDataset comprising FakeNewsAMT and Celebrity, and the same 596-item January–April 2025 Chinese-news collection. Appendix A retains coverage of the original datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 2 includes ZS, CoT, SR, SMAD and the same D2D ablations; Table 5 compares ZS, SMAD and D2D; Appendix Table 7 compares ZS and D2D.

E3.justification: Dataset filtering, sample counts, evaluation metrics, GPT-4o temperatures, default debate rounds, stage-substitution settings, and perturbation and text-length sampling procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, model substitutions by stage, speaker-order and label perturbations, debate-round sensitivity analysis, COVID-19 case study, and Appendix A error analysis are retained. The redesigned case-study figure redisplays the same evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Point-estimate and perturbation-count reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the plotted analyses and appendix results. For example, D2D's Table 2 F1 scores remain 81.97% and 81.94%, and its latest-news F1 remains 79.83% in Table 5.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 retains complementary integer scores totaling seven per dimension and the same argument that the odd aggregate total prevents ties. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The framework, multidimensional evaluation, performance, interpretability, and robustness contributions retain their meaning and scope. Removing 'robust and' from the abstract's final characterization does not withdraw the robustness claims retained in the introduction.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability boundaries are unchanged, including stage importance, text-length effects, preprocessing rationale, computational cost, text-only evidence, and dependence on pretrained knowledge.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code commitment from 'open-sourced in a future release' to 'released publicly after the official publication.' Access remains prospective in both PDFs; model settings and Appendix B prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 5 discussion are unchanged, including positioning relative to single-agent misinformation detection and existing multi-agent debate frameworks.

P1.justification: The abstract and an introductory transition receive limited wording edits, and the author/affiliation block is consolidated. Section order, substantive exposition, and appendix organization remain unchanged despite pagination shifts.

P2.justification: Two central explanatory figures are substantially redesigned. Figure 2 replaces stacked layers with orchestrator, agent, and result panels; Figure 3 replaces parallel argument columns with alternating dialogue and a separate score box. Figure 4 also moves between columns, while tables and remaining figures retain their designs.

improvement.justification: The redesigned Figure 2 makes stage-to-agent relationships and judging roles more explicit, while Figure 3 makes the debate sequence easier to follow. These provide a limited improvement in explanatory clarity. Scientific evidence and appendix documentation remain unchanged, and the revised release statement still provides only a future code commitment.
